profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 10 sits at 7375 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, Nevada, on Switch's Core Campus in unincorporated Clark County. Switch opened the building June 15, 2017, built using Switch's modular "MOD 250" construction design, roughly 350,000 square feet with up to 40 megawatts of power capacity. Switch's own opening press release states the building was constructed by a workforce of roughly 1,000 workers, 85 percent Nevada residents, over an eight-month build period, and that at the time of opening the Core Campus's three largest buildings together, Las Vegas 8, 9, and 10, totaled more than 2 million square feet and up to 315 megawatts of power. Switch's own materials place construction of Las Vegas 10 alongside the neighboring Las Vegas 11 building, together adding roughly 700,000 combined square feet to the campus. Switch markets its Core Campus today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion, a figure that has grown substantially from the 315 megawatts stated at Las Vegas 10's 2017 opening, reflecting continued campus buildout including newer AI-focused buildings. Switch does not state a formal Uptime Institute Tier certification for Las Vegas 10 specifically; the campus overall has marketed its self-created "Tier 5 Platinum" standard since 2017. Switch's Nevada tax-advantages materials describe a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement for customer equipment, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development, and Switch states 100 percent renewable energy sourcing across its Nevada campuses.

Las Vegas 10's modular "MOD 250" construction approach reflected a broader industry shift toward prefabricated, factory-assembled data center components intended to compress build timelines; Switch's own press materials specifically credited the modular design with enabling the roughly eight-month construction period. Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market, drawing additional colocation and hyperscale investment from other operators over the past decade beyond Switch alone.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 10, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 10 at 7375 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, NV. Both datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap independently give this same address, and both datacenterMap and a second directory (Baxtel) independently agree on 40 MW of capacity and 350,000 sq ft for this building. Two independent aggregator directories agree on 40 MW and 350,000 sq ft for this building, aggregator-sourced leads-only data, not confirmed by the operator, so not applied to critical_it_mw. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 10 sits on the Las Vegas Core Campus, one of five exascale campuses the operator maintains across the US, but the operator publishes no power capacity figure for this building. Two independent industry aggregator directories agree on 40 MW and 350,000 square feet for this facility, though these are leads-only sources not confirmed by Switch's own spec pages. If that 40 MW figure holds, it would represent roughly 1,000 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, though this is an external estimate rather than an operator claim.

In Nevada overall, only two facilities in this registry have published power figures from operators, totaling 10.37 MW across the state. Switch Las Vegas 10 would rank third by published megawatts in Nevada if its aggregator-sourced 40 MW were confirmed, placing it ahead of the two published sites and well above most of the state's 26 mapped facilities. Nevada has no single published figure that would place this campus or the broader Las Vegas Core Campus in the state's disclosed capacity ranking.

The facility's certification status is not published. The location, address, and capacity here reflect aggregator data, not Switch's own published specifications, which remain absent from this site's direct operator reads. Whether this site matters to AI scaling depends on whether the Las Vegas Core Campus power budget, which includes this building but is not publicly detailed, represents constrained or abundant supply relative to the broader Western grid and nearby GPU-intensive workloads.
